as_told.title: A chess champion's moves made themselves before a tournament, blamed on aliens

plain: The story is that Vasily Smyslov, a world chess champion, was in a hotel room in Germany in the 1970s, getting ready for a match against the German player Robert Hübner, when something strange happened. As he went over his moves, 'you could say an alien appeared right before him.' Kiran Ilum Xenov, the former president of a Russian republic, tells this to Michels. He says it came from Smyslov and from Smyslov's wife, Nadezhda Smyslova, and he mentions Smyslov's own records of the game. Months later, in a different interview, Michels retells it from memory without naming the player. In his version, one of the greatest chess players was playing out a practice game before a big tournament when 'the moves made themselves,' and the player put this down to 'some sort of alien intervention.' Taken at face value, it would mean something nonhuman reached into a top-level chess game.
